Inspire Partnership
The Inspire Partnership is a multi academy trust of 10 schools serving diverse communities in Croydon, Greenwich and Medway. We were formed in 2017 with the ambition to transform the lives of children through partnership and collaboration.
We believe passionately in giving every child the best possible start in life and are committed to providing rich learning experiences that ensure our young people thrive. Through our global curriculum, pupils have opportunities to learn the importance of community linked to key global themes such as sustainable development, diversity and leadership. We teach children the key knowledge and vocabulary required to succeed across the national curriculum and are proud of the impact this has in our schools.
We pride ourselves on delivering high quality and practitioner led professional development. We give our staff the best opportunities to learn and grow as professionals. The Partnership delivers a range of development programmes aimed at every level of school life. This professional support helps create the next generation of leaders and ensures we are continuously striving to improve from an evidence informed position.
Trust governance is led by our Trust Board who meet regularly and know our schools well. This work is supported strongly by Local Community Council who provide the local support and challenge for each of our schools.
If you wish to find out more about the Partnership, we would love to hear from you. You can arrange to visit any of our schools or can find more information at www.inspirepartnership.co.uk.

Maths
At Elaine Primary, we deliver a highly ambitious and inclusive mathematics curriculum designed to empower all children to become confident, competent, and resilient mathematicians. Underpinned by our commitment to social justice and educational excellence, our mastery approach ensures that every child—regardless of their starting point—develops a deep, lasting conceptual understanding of mathematics. We believe that all pupils can achieve in mathematics, and we structure our teaching sequence carefully to secure foundational fluency, eliminate cognitive overload, and push children into zones of deep mathematical reasoning and critical thinking.
Our mathematics curriculum is structured to move children systematically from concrete experiences to abstract mathematical concepts:
Securing Foundational Fluency
To reduce cognitive load and free up working memory for complex problem-solving, we place a relentless focus on securing rapid recall of fundamental number facts:
Critical Thinking and Mathematical Reasoning
Critical thinking is systematically integrated into our daily maths lessons to foster independence and analytical stamina:
Our mathematics provision is designed to close gaps immediately and ensure equitable progress for our disadvantaged cohort and pupils with SEND:
CALCULATION POLICY
Please find the calculation policy link here. This is a useful tool for parents when supporting their children at home with maths. The document takes you through each year group and the methods we use, with a step-by-step approach to teaching each of the four operations.
USEFUL LINKS
At Elaine Primary, we believe that parents and carers are our most valuable partners in securing educational excellence. When it comes to mathematics, supporting your child at home does not require you to be an expert. Instead, the most impactful thing you can do is help your child build short, daily habits of mathematical talk and play.
Our school-wide Mastery Approach is designed to eliminate cognitive overload. By practising number facts, subitising, and multiplication tables for just 5 to 10 minutes each day, you help your child automate these basic skills. This frees up their active working memory to tackle more complex mathematical reasoning and problem-solving in their daily classroom lessons.
Below is a directory of the official, school-supported digital platforms and free resources that you can use at home to support your child’s learning journey.
1. Times Tables Rock Stars (TTRS)
This is our primary digital tool for developing rapid, accurate recall of multiplication and division facts. Daily practice on TTRS is crucial, particularly for pupils in Year 3 and Year 4 as they build stamina towards the statutory National Multiplication Tables Check (MTC).
Century is an advanced, adaptive learning platform powered by artificial intelligence. It analyses your child's mathematical strengths and areas for development, creating a highly personalised study path consisting of short, micro-lessons called nuggets.
Purple Mash is a creative educational portal containing a vast suite of mathematical games, virtual manipulatives, and structured homework tasks.
4. White Rose Maths: Parent Resources
White Rose provides a wealth of free parent resources that explain the representations (such as bar models and part-part-whole diagrams) we use in the classroom.
5. 1-Minute Maths App (White Rose)
For Early Years and Key Stage 1
Created by White Rose Maths, this is a free, highly visual mobile app designed specifically for our youngest learners. It contains zero advertisements and does not require a login.
You do not need digital screens to make maths a meaningful part of your home life. Try integrating these quick, low-cost activities into your daily routines:

Global Curriculum
At Elaine Primary School, we provide pupils with a global curriculum based on knowledge and skills that is relevant for the 21st century. These skills are critically important for future success. We believe that global learning helps pupils make sense of the increasingly complex and rapidly changing world in which they live. Our curriculum enables pupils to think critically about world issues and to develop an awareness of the impact our own actions can have on others. We provide pupils with a knowledge-rich curriculum that recognises substantive and disciplinary knowledge are intrinsically linked and interdependent. Our carefully chosen content places core knowledge at the heart of each curriculum subject. The knowledge is cumulative and constructs firm foundations from EYFS which children can build conceptual understanding over time.
The six themes children are taught across the key stages are:
Children apply their core knowledge through termly projects, which are knowledge-rich, aspirational and contextualised. Children work towards authentic outcomes and engage with real-life audiences. They undertake projects that involve complex issues, and in doing so, develop an understanding of what is possible and a belief that they can make a difference. We provide rich opportunities for children to explore citizenship and real-life world issues which at times they may have to grapple with to make sense of it. This, in turn, helps them to develop skills such as collaboration and communication, thus equipping them with the necessary skills for life in the 21st century. Across each year, a number of high-quality core texts are used to bring the themes and knowledge to life for our children and to promote a connectedness with learning.

English
At Elaine, we deliver an ambitious, language-rich English curriculum that acts as a powerful vehicle for social justice and academic excellence. By equipping our pupils with exceptional reading, writing, spelling, and oracy skills, we remove barriers to learning and ensure that all children—regardless of their starting point—can communicate with clarity, confidence, and authority.
Our curriculum intent is underpinned by high-quality, culturally diverse core texts that reflect our school community, broaden horizons, and build rich cultural capital. We systematically design our teaching sequences to eliminate cognitive overload, transitioning children from early verbal mastery to advanced written composition and analytical critical thinking.
We view reading as the absolute bedrock of our entire academic offer. Our strategic reading pathway is divided into two distinct, highly aligned phases:
Early Reading and Systematic Synthetic Phonics
From their very first days in school, pupils are taught to decode with precision using the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised synthetic phonics scheme.
Key Stage 2 Comprehension and Inference
As decoding becomes automatic, we transition pupils to a whole-class reading model focused on advanced language comprehension and vocabulary acquisition.
Our writing curriculum is structured to support children to become independent, creative, and highly competent authors.
Spelling, Vocabulary, and GPS Mastery
To ensure spelling does not become a barrier to independent written expression, we follow our Spelling and Vocabulary Progression Maps, which provide a clear, coherent pathway from Year 2 to Year 6.
Fostering a Lifelong Reading Culture
We believe that being a reader is an identity that transforms lives. We celebrate this through structured school-wide routines:
The Writing Learning Journey
We want to produce confident writers who are not afraid to take risks and are able to transfer taught skills in a variety of contexts. The children will be intrinsically motivated by a clear purpose for their writing. They will be reflective writers, assessing their own and others' writing. They will have an understanding of the purpose of their writing and the impact that their word choice and style has on the reader.
Children enjoy writing and use the features of different genres and styles. They can write for different purposes and audiences. Children are proud of their writing and know that others value their writing; they see it celebrated on displays within classrooms and in shared spaces.
Supporting English & Literacy at Home:
At Elaine Primary, we believe that parents and carers are our most essential partners in helping children master the vital life skills of reading, writing, and communication. You do not need to be a literary expert to make a profound difference at home. By embedding just 5 to 10 minutes of daily talk, wordplay, and shared reading into your family routines, you help your child build the vocabulary, phonetic security, and confidence they need to succeed in the classroom.
In school, we systematically design our English curriculum to reduce cognitive load and prevent children's working memory from becoming overwhelmed. When you practice early reading and sentence building at home, you reinforce these secure foundations, making independent reading and writing a joyful and successful experience for your child.
Below is a directory of the official, school-supported digital platforms and free resources that you can use at home to support your child’s literacy journey.
For EYFS, Key Stage 1, and Targeted Catch-Up Pupils
Collins Hub is our primary digital reading platform, providing children with direct access to the exact phonetically decodable eBooks they are studying in class.
For Key Stage 2 Pupils
Serial Reader is an innovative digital platform designed to help older children build consistent, daily reading habits by delivering classic literature and engaging texts in short, manageable daily segments.
3. Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised: Parent Page
For Nursery, Reception, and Year 1 Families
To ensure complete consistency between school and home, we deliver our systematic synthetic phonics through the Little Wandle programme. The official Little Wandle parent page is packed with free, non-jargon resources.
4. Starting Reception
For Incoming Early Years Families
A successful transition into our early years setting lays the groundwork for all future academic success. We partner with Parentkind to support families in preparing their children for school life.

pageCache.text:
English as an Additional Language
Pupils with English as an additional language (EAL) are entitled to the full curriculum study. Access to learning requires attention to words and meanings embodied in each curriculum area. Meanings and understanding cannot be assumed, but must be made explicit.
Language is central to our identity. Therefore, the home language of all pupils and staff should be recognised and valued. Pupils should be encouraged to maintain their home language.
Although many pupils acquire the ability to communicate on a day to day basis in English quite quickly, the level of language needed for academic study is much deeper and more detailed, and can require continuing support for up to ten years.
Language develops best when used in purposeful contexts across the curriculum. The language demands of learning tasks need to be identified and included in planning. Teaching and support staff play a crucial role in modelling uses of language. Knowledge and skills developed in learning the first language aid the acquisition of additional languages. A clear distinction should be made between EAL and Special Educational Needs.
All EAL pupils are assessed in line with the school’s assessment procedures at Elaine. Staff have the opportunity to discuss pupils’ progress, needs and targets via weekly planning meetings, phase meetings and termly MTP reviews. Progress in the acquisition of English is regularly assessed and monitored.
Teachers and leaders use their own judgement where assessment methods are checked for cultural bias which may cause results to be inaccurate and action is taken to remove any that is identified.
Consideration and sensitivity is given to the appropriateness of testing EAL pupils at the earlier stages of English acquisition.
Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation
The curriculum is personalised and this helps the children to use their prior knowledge and experience. The speaking and listening is always the starting point of a new topic or activity and writing is always the last step. The grammatical rules and the sentence structures are taught within the context of the different topics and genres. Visual resources are used to aid their learning. The skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing are not artificially separated, but are integrated in a meaningful total experience. The children communicate with each other through paired work and group work and this way they improve their listening as well. Through speaking exercises such as interviews, storytelling and drama, the children gain verbal routine, enthusiasm and confidence. The key vocabulary is taught at the beginning of a new topic and the children learn and practise grammatical structures and sentence building using the topic vocabulary. Teachers model use of specific vocabulary and sentence stems across the curriculum which are constantly displayed and used as reference points.
The EAL teaching at Elaine focuses on individual pupil’s needs and abilities by the adults. Differentiated planning may be put into place to support the EAL children across the curriculum.
Staff use support strategies to ensure curriculum access for Pupil’s Needs:
Parental/Community Involvement
At Elaine we encourage parental and community involvement by:
Collaborative group work
Enhanced opportunities for speaking and listening
Writing frames, directed activities related to texts
Opportunities for role play
Regular feedback from staff

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI)
Equal opportunities for all Differences and similarities celebrated Involved, valued, welcomed and safe
At Elaine, we welcome everybody into our community. The staff, pupils and parents work together to make school a happy, welcoming place where all children feel that they belong and can achieve their full potential and develop as confident individuals. We celebrate diversity and promote a positive culture where everyone can thrive and feel proud of who they are. We provide a learning environment that enables all pupils to make the greatest possible progress and achieve their full potential in a caring, supportive and fully inclusive environment.
As an inclusive community, we are deeply committed to removing the barriers to learning and participation that can hinder or exclude individual pupils, or groups of pupils. Equality of opportunity is a reality for all our children within school and our dedicated inclusion team and staff work relentlessly to ensure that all children have the right to a fulfilling learning experience, regardless of their social background, ethnicity, special educational or medical need, disability, gender or religion. This includes support to all our parents, through informal coffee mornings, events and workshops, as we understand the vital role our families play in the well-being and development of their children and the importance of working together as a team.
As a school, we fully recognise our responsibilities under the Equalities Act 2010 and aim to move beyond compliance with the legislation. The vision is supported by robust equality objectives and an EDI staff and Trust working party. All staff have received training in this area and are committed to continuous improvement. We teach the children about equality, diversity and inclusion throughout our inclusive and representative global curriculum, through regular opportunities in assembly, educational visits, visitors and we aim to reflect these values in our day-to-day interactions with the children.
Everybody at Elaine is responsible for equality, diversity and inclusion, and we also have our inclusion team who are:
Headteacher and Designated Safeguarding Lead
Assistant Headteacher, SENCO and Deputy Safeguarding Lead
Home School Support Worker and Deputy Safeguarding Lead

Ofsted and Performance Information
Elaine Primary School was inspected on Wednesday 21st and Thursday 22nd of September 2022. We are pleased to share that our report has now been published and Elaine Primary School has been judged as a ‘Good’ school.
This is a huge achievement for the school and the community and a clear recognition that the hard work of all members of the school community continues to impact positively on the lives of all Elaine children. Please read the report here or see below..
Since joining the Inspire Partnership, the school has continued to go from strength to strength, where for the first time in a generation, the school has been judged as providing a good education. As a restless, ambitious school, naturally we will be working tirelessly to ensure that the next steps from the report form part of our school priorities for the remainder of this academic year and beyond and we look forward to sharing these with our school community in the coming weeks.
Whilst we are delighted with the outcome of the inspection we recognise that it is the ongoing feedback we receive from parents and children that we truly value, which enables us to ensure we provide the children of Elaine Primary School with the very best education.

Pupil Leadership
We believe the best schools have a pupil lead culture where children take on key leadership roles and get their voice heard. We wholeheartedly value the work of our pupil leaders, using it to shape the teaching and learning that happens at our school. We are moulding leaders of the future, ready for work, ready for the world. We strive to craft confident and articulate leaders who can share their views to any audience and apply their leadership skills to real life situations.
The aim of the various teams within the Pupil Leadership Team is to enable children the chance to have leadership within the school, ensuring that their voices and opinions are heard. We are a pupil lead school, regularly receiving pupil voice to make improvements. Therefore, we are giving the children the opportunity to assist with those improvements along the journey.
At Elaine, we actively encourage children to challenge, discuss and debate issues which are important to them. Our children feel safe to share their opinions and viewpoints. This is gathered through pupil voice surveys, learning walks and a pupil voice suggestion box. The feedback the junior leadership team receive from their peers is discussed at regular junior leadership team meetings and then acted upon accordingly. Members of the junior leadership team are assigned different roles and oversee their own sub teams, which are supported by a linked member of staff. These teams monitor aspects of the school including the curriculum, the behaviour and wellbeing of pupils at our school and our school environment. To align with our global curriculum, our leaders champion an eco-friendly approach to our school environments.
Junior Leadership Team (JLT)
The Junior Leadership Team (JLT) is comprised of children across the school, consisting of a range of roles and responsibilities for leading different parts of school or areas of the curriculum. Year 6 children have lead roles, overseeing sub teams as well as the overall JLT. Children across the school can then apply for a role on the JLT by submitting a letter of application to the JLT. They are then invited to interview for their preferred role where they are required to give a presentation as to why they would be the best candidate. The application and interview process encourages the children to develop their oracy skills and allows them to demonstrate their passion and commitment to the school, as well as teaching them an important life lesson.
Successful candidates work alongside members of the school’s Leadership Team and Senior Leadership Team in order to: plan and organise events, take part in monitoring and assessment of their curriculum area/key stage, promote the school at events such as the new EYFS parents meeting, support teaching and learning across the school and be role models for others.
We have sub-teams in:
Well-Being
Community
Play Leaders and Peer Mediators
Our Play Leaders are a group of elected children from KS2 classes. They are trained in participating in active play, being team plays and engaging in restorative justice. They work with the staff on the playgrounds to ensure children are happy and safe on the playgrounds. Play Leaders run games with children in the playground, along with ensuring the quiet area is engaging with quiet activities for all children to enjoy.
As a key part of our pupil leadership offer, our trained Peer Mediators play a vital role in maintaining a calm, safe, and happy environment during break times. These dedicated pupil leaders are trained in the core principles of our restorative approach. When low-level disagreements arise in the playground, our Peer Mediators step in to guide their classmates through supportive, calm conversations, helping them listen to different perspectives and co-construct positive solutions. By encouraging their peers to reflect on their feelings and find fair resolutions, they help children develop essential skills in emotional self-regulation, empathy, and collaborative problem-solving. Through this leadership role, our Peer Mediators beautifully model our school values of Excellence, Love, Aspiration, Individuality, Nurture, and Engagement, proving that small, purpose-driven actions can trigger wonderful, lasting harmony across our school.

About Us
WELCOME
Welcome to Elaine Primary School. We are delighted that you have taken the time to visit our website, and we hope it gives you a clear and engaging insight into our vibrant school life and community. As part of the Inspire Partnership, we are deeply committed to ensuring every child receives the support they need to flourish. We pride ourselves on being an inclusive, nurturing environment where curiosity is celebrated, our values are lived out daily, and every pupil is encouraged to strive for their very best.
At the heart of everything we do is our commitment to a high-quality, global curriculum. We provide our children with opportunities to explore the world around them, think critically about global issues, and understand the positive impact they can have on others. We hold high expectations for every child, creating experiences that empower them to become confident, compassionate global citizens and future agents of change.
We recognise that partnership with parents and carers is vital; you are the primary educators in your children’s lives. We strive to be an approachable, open, and collaborative school team, valuing your voice and your involvement. Whether through workshops, celebration events, or day-to-day communication, we are dedicated to building strong, trusting relationships. We know that by working together, everyone achieves more.
With our focus on strong pastoral care—through our dedicated Nurture and Pastoral support—we ensure that independence, confidence, and teamwork are woven into the fabric of our school. We are building the leaders of the future, and we strive for excellence in every endeavour.
Once again, a very warm welcome to Elaine Primary School —a school and community we are incredibly proud of.

British Values
We maintain a clear and rigorous commitment to promoting the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. At Elaine, we understand that preparing children to be active, compassionate, and responsible members of society is an essential part of our school mission. We weave our values seamlessly through our global curriculum, our trauma-informed relational practices, and our core school values of Excellence, Love, Aspiration, Individuality, Nurture, and Engagement. Through this integrated approach, we ensure that our pupils develop a deep understanding of their rights and responsibilities within modern Britain.
Democracy is a lived, daily experience at our school, driving our commitment to giving pupils a meaningful voice and genuine agency in their community. Our classroom agreements are co-constructed collaboratively by children and staff at the start of each academic year to establish respectful, harmonious, and supportive environments where everyone takes personal responsibility. Pupil leadership is structured through our democratically elected Junior Leadership Team, where children write formal proposals and deliver speeches to their peers before a class representative is chosen. Our Junior Leadership Team is highly active, taking direct responsibility for leading weekly whole-school assemblies and working alongside subject leaders to monitor and improve curriculum impact. Within our daily lessons, pupils use structured democratic tools—such as the Opinion Continuum to debate opposing viewpoints respectfully, and the Diamond Nine structure to co-operatively prioritise solutions to real-world problems. This ensures that every child knows their voice is valued, a standard reflected in our pupil surveys where children report exceptional levels of drive, safety, and trust.
At Elaine, we teach our pupils to understand that school and societal laws are established to protect us, keep us safe, and ensure our collective wellbeing. The school’s Behaviour Policy is designed around clear, predictable expectations, ensuring a calm, safe, and orderly learning environment where everyone can flourish. Pupils are actively taught our core routines—including walking sensibly and silently in transitions and utilising our whole-school attention signals—which reduces cognitive load and promotes self-regulation. In every classroom, children co-construct a maximum of five class rules that align with our ELAINE values. When rules are broken, we implement a fair, transparent graduated response. Pupils are encouraged to take responsibility for their actions through restorative practice. Using restorative conversations, staff guide pupils through a reflective process: what happened, who was affected, and how we can make things right. This ensures our community is governed by a fair, consistent, and supportive framework where children feel safe and respected
We believe that providing pupils with individual liberty is essential to cultivating self-belief, independence, and personal responsibility. Through our values-based education, we explicitly foster the value of Individuality, helping children understand that their unique characteristics and starting points are something to celebrate. In the classroom, teachers use a growth mindset approach, providing children with choices and supporting them to understand the consequences of those choices. Pupils are taught to take managed risks, develop personal resilience, and understand that challenges can be overcome. Our curriculum actively promotes pupil agency; for example, children engage in student voice surveys, shape school life through the Junior Leadership Team, and take ownership of their own emotional wellbeing using the Zones of Regulation. By equipping our pupils with the tools to self-advocate and co-construct their learning, we build confident, self-reliant citizens who value their personal freedom and respect the liberty of others
Relationships are the absolute heart of Elaine Primary School, a core principle validated by our gold-standard trauma-informed practices and the Attachment and Trauma Sensitive School Award. We explicitly teach and model mutual respect in every interaction, creating a school culture that is safe, respectful, and deeply inclusive. Our staff model positive relationships, relational warmth, and unconditional care, ensuring that children feel emotionally secure from day one. Mutual respect is woven through our curriculum, particularly in dialogic talk and collaborative learning sequences. Using structures like collaborative learning projects, pupils learn to work together, listen actively, and respect diverse viewpoints. Bullying, derogatory language, and discriminatory behaviours are never tolerated, and any incidents are dealt with swiftly and restoratively, reinforcing a shared commitment to dignity and respect for all.
TOLERANCE OF THOSE OF DIFFERENT FAITHS AND BELIEFS
At Elaine, we view our differences as a source of strength and enrichment. We explicitly teach our pupils to understand, appreciate, and celebrate different faiths, cultures, and beliefs. Our broad and balanced curriculum includes dedicated Religious Education and RHE sequences that explore diverse world-views. This is supported by our weekly assemblies, which strategically recognise and celebrate a wide range of global events and festivals, such as Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Navratri, and Diwali, alongside cultural events like European Languages Day. Through our structured critical thinking tools—including Perspective Glasses to explore how others see the world and the Opinion Continuum to debate issues respectfully—we teach children how to engage constructively with beliefs different from their own. This fosters an exceptional climate of tolerance and mutual understanding, ensuring all pupils grow into open-minded citizens ready to contribute positively to modern, multicultural Britain.
